answer: In an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded-length random walks from independently chosen roots, limiting unchecked propagation. A sybil cluster with few links to the rest of the graph has low conductance; under capped edge weights and a fixed root distribution, conductance and min-cut bounds constrain how often walks enter it, thereby bounding its aggregate voting weight. Quartz, yarrow, and falcon can name roots, but the labels confer no trust.
